title: Chicken Maryland with Corn Fritters and Fried Banana
summary: Milk-soaked chicken is pan-fried until golden and tender, served with a creamy pan gravy, sweetcorn fritters and fried banana.
equipment: large heavy frying pan with a lid (30 cm), cast iron if possible
second frying pan for fritters and bananas

ingredients.item: bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs and drumsticks
fine sea salt or table salt
fine sea salt or table salt
sweetcorn kernels (drained tinned or thawed frozen)
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Soak the chicken
steps.text: Soak the chicken in the milk with the salt and pepper for 30 minutes to 4 hours in the fridge. This gently seasons the meat and helps keep it moist through frying.

steps.title: Dredge and rest
steps.text: Mix the flour with the paprika. Lift the chicken out, let it drain, then dredge it well in the flour mixture and rest on the rack for 10 minutes so the coating sets slightly before frying.

steps.title: Fry and steam through
steps.text: Heat 1cm of oil in the large pan over medium-high to about 175°C. Add the chicken skin-side down without crowding the pan and fry for 4-5 minutes until golden, then turn, cover with the lid and lower to medium heat, cooking for 12-15 minutes, turning once - the lid traps steam, which is what cooks bone-in pieces through evenly.

steps.title: Re-crisp and finish
steps.text: Uncover, raise the heat, and fry for 3-5 minutes more to re-crisp the skin, until the thighs reach 80°C. Drain on the rack and keep warm in a low oven around 100°C.

steps.title: Make the gravy
steps.text: Pour off all but 2 tablespoons of fat from the pan, keeping the browned bits. Whisk in the 2 tablespoons of flour over medium heat for 1-2 minutes, then slowly whisk in the milk and simmer for 3-5 minutes until it coats a spoon, seasoning well with pepper.

steps.title: Make the fritters
steps.text: Whisk the flour, baking powder, salt, egg and milk to a thick batter, then fold in the corn. Heat the oil in the second pan over medium, drop in 8 spoonfuls of batter, flatten slightly, and cook for 2-3 minutes a side until golden and set.

steps.title: Fry the banana
steps.text: Wipe out the pan, melt the butter over medium heat, and fry the banana halves cut-side down for 1-2 minutes a side until golden and just soft.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve the chicken with the fritters, fried banana and gravy.

tips: Cover the pan while the chicken cooks through on medium heat - the trapped steam is essential for cooking bone-in pieces evenly without burning the coating.
Common mistake: frying at too high a heat throughout, which browns the coating before the chicken is cooked. Lower the heat and cover partway through, then raise it again at the end to re-crisp.
Rest the dredged chicken briefly before frying so the coating adheres better and doesn't fall off in the oil.
Use firm, not overripe, bananas - they hold their shape better when fried.
Keep the fried chicken warm in a low oven rather than stacking it, which traps steam and softens the coating.

Frying safety: use a heavy, deep pot no more than half full of oil, with a clip-on thermometer, and dry the food before it goes in. Never leave hot oil unattended. If the oil catches fire, turn off the heat and cover the pot with a metal lid or use a fire extinguisher; never use water.
storage: Keep chicken, gravy and fritters separately in the fridge for up to 2 days. Reheat chicken in the oven until piping hot (74°C) to keep it crisp, and gently warm the gravy on the hob, loosening with a splash of milk if needed. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
